Author: Samit Gopal

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:46145

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Cancellation Application No. - 8524 of 2016
Applicant :- State of U.P.
Opposite Party :- Lalta Prasad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- G.A.
Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J.
1.
Heard Sri Virendra Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the State/applicant.
Sri Vipul Shukla appears on behalf of opposite party Lalta Prasad and files his Vakalatnama today in Court, which is taken on record.

2. The present bail cancellation application has been filed by the State with the following prayers:-
"It is, therefore, most respectfylly prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to set-aside and cancel the bail order dated 08.10.2015 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (E.C.), Court no.21, Shahjahanpur, granting bail to the accused opposite party Lalta Prasad in Case crime no. 680 of 2015, Under Sections 323, 504, 376, 342, 498-A of IPC and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Nigohi, District Shahjahanpur, and it is further prayed that the opposite parties may State Of U.P. vs Lalta Prasad on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192674899/
1 be taken into custody forthwith, otherwise, the interest of the State will be frustrated.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (E.C.), Court no.21, Shahjahanpur
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: State Of U.P. vs Lalta Prasad
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
And/Or pass such other and further order which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case."
3. At the very outset, learned counsel for the State submits that order granting bail to the opposite party, although, does not contain any observation of the court concerned regarding the statements of the victim recorded during investigation but looking to the fact that bail has been granted to the opposite party vide order dated 8.10.2015 and it is now more than eight years and the trial is still pending, it would be expedient in the interest of justice that appropriate orders be passed directing the trial court to expedite the trial and conclude the same as expeditiously as possible.
4.

Considering the limited argument of learned counsel for the applicant State, the present application for cancellation of bail is disposed of with the direction to the trial court to conclude the trial of the present case as expeditiously as possible.

5. It is directed that the trial of the aforesaid case pending before the concerned trial court be concluded, as expeditiously as possible, strictly in accordance with Section 309 Cr.P.C. and in view of the principles as has been laid down in the judgement of Apex Court in the cases of Shailendra Kumar Vs. State of Bihar: (2002) 1 SCC 655; Vinod Kumar Vs. State of Punjab: (2015) 3 SCC 220,
Hussain and Another Vs. Union of India: (2017) 5 SCC 702 ; Rajesh Yadav Vs. State of U.P. :
Criminal Appeal No. 339-340 of 2014 and the order dated 30.09.2022 passed in Special Leave Petition (Criminal) Diary No. 8905/2022 ; Mukesh Singh Vs. The State of Uttar Pradesh and another), subject to any legal impediment.
6. The bail cancellation application is disposed of with the aforesaid directions.
Order Date :- 14.3.2024 Aiman (Samit Gopal, J.)
